r10-decomposition-legitimacy.title: Is the productive-invocation decomposition legitimate or post-hoc
r10-decomposition-legitimacy.imperative: Check the productive-invocation arithmetic (attempts minus help reads = 16/16 CLI vs 18/17 MCP averaging 18) against the raw records, and render a direct verdict on Commander's central question: is stripping one-off --help reads a legitimate, principled decomposition of the counting unit, or is it post-hoc reasoning adopted only because the raw totals stopped supporting the pre-existing negative conclusion once the loop fix moved them toward the door? State the verdict plainly, with reasoning. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r10-decomposition-legitimacy.finding: Direct answer to Commander's central question: I judge the productive-invocation decomposition to have real post-hoc characteristics, not fabricated but reached for. Evidence, not just timing-correlation: (1) The write-up's OWN revision note and Commander's rework handoff both state on the record that the ORIGINAL basis for the DC5 negative was 'the spreads overlap completely' (raw totals, CLI [18,21] vs MCP [17,19]) -- confirmed by grep across crew-handoffs/g4-reviewer-handoff.md, g4-reviewer-result.md and g4-review/review.json: 'overlap' appears repeatedly describing the pre-fix argument, 'productive' appears NOWHERE in any attempt-1 artifact. The productive/help-reads split is new to this rework, introduced only after the loop fix flipped the raw-total comparison to favor the door (CLI 22.0 > MCP 18.0, non-overlapping -- a PASS on the pre-registered metric). (2) The counting unit was explicitly fixed BEFORE the arms ran ('One invocation attempt... however packaged') as the PRIMARY, pre-registered metric -- exactly the kind of commitment meant to prevent picking a different metric after seeing the data. 'Productive invocations' (attempts minus help-reads) is a different, not-pre-registered unit. (3) Construct-validity problem, independent of timing: DC5 tests whether the door reduces spine-management cost INCLUDING fumbling/lookup friction (the counting unit explicitly includes client-rejected and malformed calls as cost). Help-reads are the CLI arm's own text elsewhere credits as avoiding fumbles ('it read the help first and then got it right') -- i.e. help-reads are a manifestation of exactly the friction a self-documenting typed door is supposed to eliminate. Stripping that category out before comparing is close to excluding the effect under test, not a neutral secondary lens. (4) Selective application: score_arm.py reports THREE legitimate lenses -- raw invocation attempts (door wins, 18 vs 22), productive invocations (CLI wins, 16 vs 18), and tool_calls_carrying_them/'acts of attention' (CLI wins big, 10 vs 18-19, and THIS one WAS already a headline metric in the original pre-fix write-up per the original handoff's close-criterion #1 table, so it is not itself post-hoc). The write-up picks the two lenses that support the pre-existing negative conclusion (productive + acts-of-attention) and explicitly discounts the one lens that doesn't (raw totals, recast as 'onboarding cost, not spine-management cost') -- the discounting is exactly backwards from a neutral read, since raw totals is the PRE-REGISTERED metric and the other two are ex-post reframings, yet the write-up treats it the other way around. What is legitimate: the arithmetic is correct (independently verified: 21-5=16, 23-7=16, 19-0=19, 17-0=17, matches the table exactly) and fully disclosed, not hidden; the onboarding-vs-recurring distinction is a real, bounded, honestly-labeled forward-looking observation about longer spines. What is not legitimate: presenting that decomposition as THE verdict that displaces the pre-registered primary metric's result, rather than as a secondary caveat on a verdict the primary metric now actually supports as a PASS. RECOMMENDATION: report the pre-registered raw-invocation-attempts result as the primary DC5 finding (which is now a PASS, not a negative) and demote the productive/onboarding-cost analysis to an explicitly-labeled secondary extrapolation about longer spines, not the load-bearing verdict. This is a blocking finding per the handoff's own governing rule ('a decomposition you judge post-hoc are all blocking findings').
